## Multiple Choice Questions

**1.** The correlation coefficient between two monthly accounting measures is −0.80. What does this indicate?

A.  They are unrelated, because a negative coefficient means no relationship.
B.  The first measure is, on average, 80 percent smaller than the second.
C.  A rise in one measure causes the other to fall.
D.  They move strongly in opposite directions along a straight line.

**2.** Removing a single unusual month from a data set changes the correlation between revenue and the number of customers from strong to weak. What should an analyst do?

A.  Investigate the month, and report both results unless it can be explained.
B.  Report the weaker correlation, because unusual months should always be deleted.
C.  Report neither, because correlation cannot be used with monthly data.
D.  Report the stronger correlation, because it uses more of the data.

**3.** A regression of monthly revenue on a month index reports an R Square of 0.17. What does this mean?

A.  Revenue grows by about 17 percent from one month to the next.
B.  The fitted line explains about 17 percent of the variation in monthly revenue.
C.  The slope has a 17 percent chance of being zero in the population.
D.  The forecast will be accurate to within 17 percent of actual revenue.

**4.** Fitted to all thirty-six months, the slope of Charles River's revenue trend has a p-value of about 0.01. Fitted without the start-up month, the p-value is about 0.07. What is the best conclusion?

A.  Revenue has a strong upward trend that should be extended into the forecast.
B.  The start-up month should be kept, because it makes the result significant.
C.  The trend depends on one unusual month, so there is no reliable evidence of one.
D.  A p-value above 0.05 proves that revenue will not grow in the coming year.

**5.** What is a backtest of a forecasting method?

A.  Recalculating a forecast after the period and replacing it with the actual amount
B.  Fitting it to earlier data and comparing its forecasts of held-back later data with the actuals
C.  Forecasting the past by running the method backward from the latest period
D.  Checking that the forecast formulas contain no errors before the forecast is used

**6.** Why should a new forecasting method be compared with simple benchmarks, such as the mean or the value of the same quarter last year?

A.  Excel cannot calculate forecasts more complex than the benchmarks.
B.  Benchmarks are always more accurate than more elaborate methods.
C.  Auditing standards require every forecast to be compared with the mean.
D.  A method that cannot beat them is not worth its extra complexity.

**7.** How do TREND and FORECAST.LINEAR differ?

A.  Both fit a least-squares line; TREND can return several values at once, FORECAST.LINEAR one.
B.  FORECAST.LINEAR requires the Data Analysis ToolPak, while TREND does not.
C.  TREND works only with dates, while FORECAST.LINEAR works only with numbers.
D.  TREND fits a curved line, while FORECAST.LINEAR fits a straight line.

**8.** What is a flexible budget?

A.  A budget that managers may change during the year without approval
B.  The static budget with every amount increased by the same percentage
C.  The budget recalculated at actual volume with the budgeted prices and unit costs
D.  The actual results rearranged in the format and order of the budget

**9.** What does the sales-volume variance measure?

A.  The difference between the actual and the budgeted fixed costs
B.  The effect of actual selling prices differing from the budgeted prices
C.  The effect on margin of selling more or fewer units than planned, at planned margins
D.  The effect of producing more units than were sold in the period

**10.** Actual sales commission expense is 75 percent below the static budget, and actual revenue is far below the budgeted revenue. What is the best interpretation?

A.  The sales team cut its commission rates, which saved the company money.
B.  Most of it reflects lower revenue, so flex the budget before judging the rest.
C.  Part of the commission expense was never recorded in the ledger.
D.  Commissions are a fixed cost, so the whole difference is a spending variance.

**11.** A company has fixed costs of $900,000 and a contribution margin ratio of 30 percent. What is its break-even revenue?

A.  $270,000
B.  $1,170,000
C.  $2,700,000
D.  $3,000,000

**12.** What does Goal Seek do?

A.  It finds the value of one input that makes a formula cell equal a target.
B.  It shows a formula's result for every value in a range of one or two inputs.
C.  It compares the results of several named sets of input values in a report.
D.  It maximizes or minimizes a result subject to several constraints on its inputs.

**13.** An analyst wants to see how the difference in contribution changes for every combination of three discount rates and nine volume increases. Which tool fits best?

A.  Goal Seek
B.  A two-variable data table
C.  A one-variable data table
D.  The Correlation tool of the ToolPak

**14.** A production-mix model is solved with Solver's Simplex LP method. Under what condition can Solver also produce a Sensitivity report with shadow prices?

A.  When every variable cell is required to be a whole number
B.  When the model is solved with the Evolutionary method instead
C.  When it finds an optimum and the model has no integer constraints
D.  Only when the model has a single constraint on its variable cells

**15.** Why does a documentation table for a model's assumptions include a sensitivity column?

A.  To show which assumptions change the conclusion most, so review focuses on them
B.  To prove that the assumptions used in the model are correct
C.  To record the formula used in each cell of the model
D.  To list the people who approved each assumption and when
